name: Anarcho-Communism
summary: Anarcho-communism seeks a stateless society in which the means of production are held in common and goods are distributed by need rather than through wages, money or markets. It organises life through free federations of communes and workers' associations, reaches it through social revolution and direct action, and rejects both capitalism and the Marxist-Leninist state.
scope: The classical movement from Déjacque, Cafiero and Kropotkin through Malatesta, Berkman and Makhno, based on Kropotkin's The Conquest of Bread, Malatesta's Anarchy, Berkman's What Is Communist Anarchism and the Wikipedia overview. It does not cover individualist anarchism, anarcho-syndicalism as a distinct union programme, or council communism, which have their own profiles.

furtherReading.title: The Conquest of Bread, by Peter Kropotkin
furtherReading.note: The founding statement of how a free communist society would feed and house everyone.

furtherReading.title: Anarchy, by Errico Malatesta
furtherReading.note: A short, readable dialogue-style case against government and for free agreement.

furtherReading.title: What Is Communist Anarchism?, by Alexander Berkman
furtherReading.note: A plain introduction for working-class readers.

keyFigures.name: Peter Kropotkin
keyFigures.role: Russian theorist who gave anarchist communism its main statement in The Conquest of Bread.

keyFigures.name: Errico Malatesta
keyFigures.role: Italian anarchist who developed and popularised the case for abolishing government.

keyFigures.name: Alexander Berkman
keyFigures.role: Author of the popular introduction What Is Communist Anarchism? and critic of the Bolshevik state.

sources.title: Anarcho-communism
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Overview of aims, thinkers, property and distribution, work obligations, nationalism, family, and the platformist, synthesist and insurrectionary strands. First 100,000 characters read.

sources.title: The Conquest of Bread
sources.author: Peter Kropotkin
sources.usedFor: Expropriation, wages and distribution by need, communism without government, free agreement, division of labour, decentralised agro-industrial communes. Preface to chapter 4 and chapters 11 to 14 read.

sources.title: Anarchy
sources.author: Errico Malatesta
sources.usedFor: Government as the gendarme of property, voting and majorities, force and defence, crime and punishment, army, religion, education, free compact. Read to the middle of chapter 9.

sources.title: What Is Communist Anarchism?
sources.author: Alexander Berkman
sources.usedFor: Exploitation of wage labour, property, war and patriotism, crime and social conditions, and the critique of Leninist dictatorship. Read to the middle of chapter 8.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Exchange value and commerce are rejected outright; Kropotkin's alternative to both market and state is free agreement and distribution by need.

public-ownership.rationale: Means of production should be held in common, but run by communes and workers' federations; state ownership is just another employer-boss and is rejected.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation belongs to the state they want abolished and they seek expropriation of wealth, not higher rates; they would not oppose it as a tactic but it is not their programme.

unions-good.rationale: Anarcho-communists generally back workers' organisation and strikes, but an anti-organisational wing distrusted unions, so the strands are split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Private ownership of land and instruments of labour is the root of wage exploitation; Berkman, citing Proudhon, calls the possessions of the rich stolen property.

regulate-corporations.rationale: They want corporations expropriated and the state abolished, so state regulation is seen as a government protecting property owners rather than a solution.

cut-welfare.rationale: Distribution by need is central; cutting support for the poor contradicts mutual aid, even though they distrust welfare delivered by the state.

worker-ownership.rationale: The instruments of labour are common property held by the workers' associations and communes; this is a founding demand.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Government is seen as an apparatus of force protecting privilege, so granting it more power over individuals is rejected whatever the pretext.

strong-leader.rationale: Malatesta's whole case is against government; a leader who bypasses checks is the opposite of free agreement.

state-harmful.rationale: Kropotkin aims "to abolish the State, the personification of injustice, oppression, and monopoly"; Malatesta calls for abolition of government.

empower-police-military.rationale: Police, courts and standing armies are treated as tools of the property owners; Kropotkin counts them as wasteful expense and Malatesta wants them gone.

decide-locally.rationale: Society is organised as free federations of communes built from the bottom up; Kropotkin's "free agro-industrial communes" decide for themselves.

rehabilitation.rationale: Malatesta would treat offenders as "the sick brother needing treatment" and Berkman blames social conditions for crime; prisons themselves are rejected.

traditional-family.rationale: Déjacque opposed the nuclear family and anarchists reject authority within marriage, though Kropotkin also criticised communes run as one family; not a central issue.

more-religion-public.rationale: Malatesta lists the priest among the "traders in lies" and Berkman says church and school side with rulers.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Equal solidarity of all the oppressed is assumed and they back direct action against discrimination, but remedies through state programmes are not their approach.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Patriotism is opposed as a tool of state and militarism; local cultural variety is welcomed but national preservation is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: Anarcho-communists advocate social revolution and expropriation, not the gradual reform of established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Opposition to nation-states and borders and an emphasis on international solidarity make restriction contrary to principle.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International state bodies are more government; they favour federation from below instead.

free-trade.rationale: Commerce is itself rejected; free trade is not endorsed though they also oppose protective state tariffs.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotism is opposed on equality grounds and as support for militarism and state loyalty.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: State armies are distrusted and Malatesta says war loses its cause without governments; volunteer solidarity is accepted but state intervention is not.

open-borders.rationale: Communes would federate "irrespectively of national frontiers" and the nation-state is abolished.

limit-growth.rationale: Kropotkin wanted less waste and shorter labour hours but also abundance for all; adherents differ on growth and modern ecological strands split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Kropotkin was optimistic about technology for reducing toil but tied it to social change, so adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Social revolution and expropriation are the stated means; Kropotkin says the real work of revolution begins after government falls.

experts-over-public.rationale: Authority of any elite is rejected and Malatesta stresses administration as delegated work, not power.

central-planning.rationale: They reject an authoritarian state plan; Kropotkin's communes coordinate through free agreement and federation, not a central authority.

socialized-markets.rationale: Cafiero and Kropotkin reject exchange and wages even where owned collectively; Kropotkin rejected collectivist remuneration as well.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land should be held in common, not taxed; a tax presupposes the state and market in land.

basic-income.rationale: Distribution by need goes beyond an income, but a payment from the state and use of money are rejected.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tied to the nation-state, patriotism and capital; contrary to internationalism.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Direction by a state is rejected; production is decided by federated communes.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property is held in common; personal possessions are kept but small owners' means of production are not the goal.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Cafiero called for abolishing wage labour and Dézamy wanted money abolished; Kropotkin says a new form of property needs a new form of remuneration.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale argues against its value: it rests on abolishing money altogether, not a free market in money.

reviewHistory.rationale: They would abolish central banks as part of abolishing money, but not leave money to the market.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its own rationale argues against its value: it rests on abolishing money altogether, not a free market in money.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies bargaining wages and prices contradict anti-statism and the abolition of wages.

one-party-rule.rationale: Berkman says Leninist principles can only lead to dictatorship and reaction.

democracy-best.rationale: Malatesta argues majority numbers prove neither reason nor justice, yet anarcho-communists favour direct democracy; they reject representative government.

direct-votes.rationale: Direct democracy is favoured over representation, but Malatesta doubts majority rule, so they prefer free agreement.

workers-councils.rationale: Federated workers' councils are a model for organising society, though communes rather than councils alone are the base.

natural-rulers.rationale: Malatesta defines government as a minority holding power over the rest and argues it serves the property owners, so no group has a natural title to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Malatesta defends the right of defence and calls for revolutionary action against those who own wealth.

war-builds-character.rationale: Berkman describes war as organised violence waged for capitalist profit with workers paying the price, leaving no room for it as character-building.

separate-church-state.rationale: They oppose both institutions and want the state abolished, so favour separation but would go further.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts and policing as services sold for profit are rejected; they want defence through voluntary popular organisation.

military-superiority.rationale: Anarcho-communists oppose patriotism partly for its ties to militarism, so a national drive for military superiority is rejected.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Patriotism and the nation-state are opposed on equality grounds, so organising a state around one ethnic group is the opposite of their view.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class struggle is central to their analysis of exploitation, though they do not use Marx's historical materialism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Distribution by need and common ownership aim at equal enjoyment of the product, though not identical rewards.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Opposes imperialism but state-to-state payments are not their approach; no stated position.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nations or civilisations uniting politically is state-building, which they oppose.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kropotkin stresses mutual aid and solidarity rather than self-interest as an ethical basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: They reject duties imposed by authority, though stressing solidarity and each doing a share.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Kropotkin wanted to reorganise industry through decentralisation, not abandon it; primitivists are a different strand.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Handing decisions to an unaccountable system is a form of government by experts, which they oppose.

restore-past-order.rationale: They seek a new society, not restoration, and Kropotkin criticised earlier communes.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Malatesta presents anarchy as a method of free initiative, not a blueprint, but they remain firmly committed to principle.

direct-action.rationale: Direct action rather than parliament is the stated method; Malatesta calls the vote's benefit "entirely derisory."

means-match-ends.rationale: Anarchists, including Berkman, say revolution must prefigure the free society; Berkman warns Leninist methods lead to dictatorship.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Kropotkin's plan relies on advanced agro-industrial communes with reduced labour hours, not on abandoning farming and industry.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kropotkin attacks specialisation ("the eighteenth part of a pin") and wants an end to the brain/manual split.

distribute-by-need.rationale: "From each according to ability, to each according to needs" is the guiding principle; Kropotkin says "Take what you need."

production-for-use.rationale: Kropotkin judges production by whether it meets human needs with the least waste of energy.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Berkman says workers receive a fraction of what they produce, the rest taken as rent, profit and interest.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Berkman says Marxist and Leninist principles lead only to dictatorship and reaction.

collective-farming.rationale: Land is held in common and Kropotkin's communes combine agriculture and industry, but this is through voluntary communes.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Berkman argues wars serve capitalist profit and that financiers pressed the US into war.

taxation-theft.rationale: Opponents of the state, but their critique of exploitation is aimed at profit and rent, and they differ from propertarians on what taxes take.

harm-principle.rationale: No explicit endorsement; Malatesta stresses defence against aggression but rejects law as such, so the principle is not framed that way.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Communism stresses collective ownership and solidarity, so rights are not framed as individual only.

conscription.rationale: State armies are rejected; Malatesta says a free people defends itself voluntarily.

exit-over-voice.rationale: They want direct participation, not mere exit, though freedom to leave a commune is accepted.

state-as-business.rationale: Malatesta rejects government itself and the profit motive behind the property system, so running the state like a firm serving customers is doubly alien.

positive-liberty.rationale: Kropotkin's right to well-being and Berkman's view that wage bargains are not free make material means a condition of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Malatesta says teachers and priests shape minds toward obedience, but the claim that they outrank elected officials is not theirs; they hold capital and state power central.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The ideology holds that behaviour is shaped by socialisation and mode of production, not fixed nature.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation of any kind is rejected in favour of direct federated organisation.

total-state.rationale: The abolition of government is the defining aim, so a state directing every area of life is its exact opposite.

national-rebirth.rationale: The ideology rejects nationalism and the idea of building loyalty to a nation-state, so a project of national rebirth has no appeal.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule resting on oaths between lords and followers is a hierarchy of command; Malatesta wants authority-free arrangement by free compact.

bound-labor.rationale: Kropotkin ties the wage system to private ownership of land and tools and wants those relations ended, so legal bondage to a lord is a form of the monopoly he attacks.

universal-morality.rationale: Kropotkin grounded ethics in mutual aid as a natural tendency, but there is no stated position on universal moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Malatesta notes that "a thousand minorities" each think they are right, and prefers pluralist free agreement.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The ideology opposes nation-states, so a state for any nation is rejected in principle, though adherents distinguish this from Jewish persecution and support the safety of all peoples.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Opposition to borders favours free movement for everyone, but a nation's special right of return to its homeland is a nationalist framing they do not use.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Workers' councils and common ownership give workers direct control; they would go further and abolish the employer-employee relation.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom as property and market rights is rejected; though freedom is tied to economic equality.

national-self-determination.rationale: They oppose the nation-state and patriotism, though they accept communes governing themselves; a national state for each nation is not the aim.

force-without-un.rationale: State armies are opposed as instruments of power, so a government sending force abroad on its own authority is not supported.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Anti-religious, with Malatesta calling people "stupefied by superstition"; emotion is not rejected.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Need, not citizenship, is the basis of distribution, and borders are rejected.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Makhno and others held able adults should work and Kropotkin accepted expulsion of non-contributors, but Kropotkin hoped voluntary; adherents are split.

class-collaboration.rationale: Berkman presents employers as taking most of what workers produce as rent, profit and interest, so partnership between the two is a false picture.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: They do not call for destruction of cultural institutions; Kropotkin wants all to have access to libraries.

workers-nation.rationale: Internationalism is part of the ideology, with federations that cross national frontiers.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Hierarchy and fixed roles are rejected, and Déjacque attacked the traditional family.

ban-interest.rationale: Berkman lists interest among extractions, but they abolish money rather than legislating against interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Malatesta rejects law as a tool of the privileged and international solidarity cuts against racial division.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Malatesta describes government as the property owners' gendarme, a direct statement of this view.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The nation-state and its national culture are not something they ask newcomers to join; open federation of peoples is the model.

elite-replacement.rationale: Nothing in the ideology supports a conspiracy about immigration; it favours open borders and solidarity.

proportional-representation.rationale: Malatesta calls the vote's benefit for workers entirely derisory, so a fairer way of electing parliaments is a minor reform at best.

national-mission.rationale: Anarcho-communists reject patriotism and imperial promotion of any state's system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Opposes hierarchy including the family, though class is primary in classical texts; Goldman and later anarcha-feminists strengthen the claim.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Malatesta says elections favour the best deceivers and that government serves property owners.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Coercive state control of reproduction is the kind of government power they abolish; Malatesta would treat deviance as a matter of care.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Malatesta says government is the gendarme of property, so a minimal state protecting property is exactly what they oppose.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equality and internationalism rule out racial hierarchy and social pressure on families.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Kropotkin's mutual aid and equality of all are basic, and Berkman says wealth belongs to society.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Malatesta wants no state coercion over minds, and the Church is among the forces he opposes, so a law against conversion is opposed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Malatesta says teachers and priests are used to shape obedience; they would keep religious instruction out of schools, though they reject state schools too.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Berkman says Marxist-Leninist principles lead to dictatorship; anarchists want the state abolished immediately.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Free agreement is the basis, though they go beyond "authority" by rejecting government.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist national economics belongs to the state-and-capital system they reject; the commune federations are not concerned with national export balances.

population-transfer.rationale: Forcing out a minority is incompatible with equality and the free association of all.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Malatesta defends defence only, but expropriation of owners is justified as revolution, so adherents see force against property owners as defence of society.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Kropotkin's thesis in mutual aid is that cooperation, not struggle, drives progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They oppose giving governments new coercive powers and reject parliaments, so outlawing groups is rejected even if the targets are hostile.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Malatesta and Berkman critique wage dependence and government as domination.

separated-powers.rationale: They want government abolished, not balanced, so checks among state bodies are only a lesser evil.

vanguard-party.rationale: Berkman rejects Leninist methods; platformists want organisation but not a ruling party.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Kropotkin makes everyone's needs the first claim on production and starts from the poor, though the ideology means to end poverty by equal provision.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Kropotkin wants housing taken according to each family's need, not sold; the policy is a market mechanism they would not value.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Berkman and the movement treat strikes and workers' organisation as the weapons of the exploited, so legal restriction is opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Kropotkin argues that want arises from social organisation, noting peasants lack food even where not overproduced.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The ideology builds on solidarity across nations and groups and sees cooperation as natural to all.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Malatesta's critique is that government rests on force against the people, so extending that power in a crisis is rejected.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State price-setting is government, but they would ensure food distribution by need.

party-commands-army.rationale: A ruling party and an army are both organs of the dictatorship Berkman criticises in the Bolshevik regime.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship and borders are state devices they want abolished, so lengthening the wait is the wrong direction.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Déjacque wanted democratised offices; they favour delegates not paid above workers, though prefer abolition.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Platformists favour unity while insurrectionists and synthesists reject it; split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They favour federation from below between communes across frontiers, not a union among states, so only partial sympathy.

church-by-bishops.rationale: They oppose hierarchy and the priest's role in enslaving minds, as Malatesta puts it.

clerical-rule.rationale: Malatesta lists the priest among the traders in lies, so rule by religious scholars is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Malatesta opposes government control of minds, and censorship by moral guardians is that control.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Offices of rule are to be abolished, so term limits matter little; the leader's grip on power is the target.

recall-officials.rationale: Direct democracy with delegates removable by those who chose them is the anarchist alternative to representation.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Kropotkin says houses taken according to need of each family, not ownership by each.

people-in-arms.rationale: Malatesta says a people who want to defend their country are invincible, citing volunteers.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Kropotkin wants integration of agriculture and industry, not preferring rural life.

death-penalty.rationale: Malatesta would treat offenders as the sick brother needing treatment and Berkman blames conditions, so execution is rejected.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Malatesta describes people stupefied by superstition and priests among the traders in lies, so promoting creationism is opposed.

restrict-pornography.rationale: State censorship of adults is rejected, though some strands criticise commodified sex; no direct source.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The nation-state and its membership rules are rejected; descent is the exclusion they oppose.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They oppose general law and the Church alike, so special exemptions by the state are neither valued nor central.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Abolition of private property and the wage system is the core demand; formal political change without it is insufficient.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Malatesta doubts elected assemblies and majority rule; they would prefer popular self-organisation to a body writing a constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Berkman denounces dictatorship and says means must fit ends, so suspending freedom for development is rejected.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: They oppose militarism and state armies, so a national nuclear arsenal is rejected.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: They reject heads of state; a direct election is a lesser evil among options they do not choose.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Money is to be abolished and economic coordination replaced by free federations, so independent central banks are not a goal.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: They reject nationalism and territorial claims by states, so insisting on a historic homeland is against their view.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rejects private property of means of production rather than limiting it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Berkman rejects Bolshevik dictatorship; anarchists often called it state capitalism.

collective-defense.rationale: State alliances are linked to militarism, which they oppose.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They want the Church's power ended but not by placing it under a state they also oppose.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A head of state is a ruler; the ideology does not accept one at all.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Free association and federation mean parts may leave; Malatesta stresses free compact.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

reviewHistory.rationale: The question concerns larger states; communes' autonomy is valued but joining a state is not their model.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-12): its rationale rests on general self-government, separate laws or no stated position, not on keeping a distinct economic system, and the statement now asks only whether a region joining a larger state should be free to keep its economic system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Malatesta rejects government and the priests who bless it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Taxes and money are to be abolished; a flat rate would still fall on workers.

character-from-environment.rationale: The ideology rejects a fixed human nature and holds that behaviour is shaped by socialisation and mode of production; Berkman blames conditions for crime.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Malatesta wants government abolished, so an unbound ruler is clearly rejected, though he does not address this statement.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Government by the few or many in any mix is rejected for abolition of government.

leader-cult.rationale: Honouring a leader as the nation's embodiment contradicts their anti-authority stance and opposition to patriotism.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Berkman argues that Bolshevik rule created a new ruling group, and anarchists hold that any state keeps class domination.

land-redistribution.rationale: Expropriation of land is central, though they want it held in common by communes rather than given to individuals.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Nationalism and territorial claims by states are rejected.

common-currency.rationale: They want money abolished, so a shared currency is irrelevant at best.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Uniting peoples by ancestry is nationalism, which they reject; solidarity is meant across all peoples.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Anarchists differ from Marx and often stress moral and social factors alongside the economy; adherents are split.

ban-cartels.rationale: They want common ownership, not a competition law; breaking up cartels leaves private property intact.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Malatesta argues that majority numbers prove neither reason nor justice and that minorities are sacrificed.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Governing bodies are to be abolished; quotas within them are a reform not sought.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: They favour federations across frontiers; autarky for a state and colonies is not their model.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Treaties among states are a state tool; no stated position on standards.

moral-incentives.rationale: Kropotkin expects voluntary work, sustained by interest in work and solidarity.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Insurrectionist anarcho-communists backed propaganda of the deed while platformists and others looked to mass movements, so adherents split.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Privilege rests on wealth and ownership of land, and they would abolish it with property and government.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Patriotism is opposed, so teaching history with the nation at the centre is not endorsed.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Berkman and the movement oppose imperialism and rule by one people over others.

patriotic-education.rationale: Patriotism is opposed as a means of binding people to the state.

public-money-creation.rationale: They want money abolished; changing who issues it leaves the system standing.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Kropotkin expects crisis and revolution rather than adaptation.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial influence is opposed as a state project.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Berkman describes workers as broadly exploited, so a privileged upper stratum is not part of the classical picture.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Property rights as a basis for exclusion are rejected; Kropotkin's principle is need and equal access.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: They reject law and the state as guarantors of liberty, but have no statement on constitutional rights.

elective-rulers.rationale: They reject rulers, elected or not; Malatesta says elections favour those best at deceiving the public.

minority-veto.rationale: Malatesta argues majorities do not prove justice and sacrifice minorities, and free agreement means no one is bound without consent; some accept majority decisions in practice.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: They support resistance to rulers generally, so agree even though they go further than the constitutional framing.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Malatesta says the vote strengthened bourgeois power, so parliaments are not the answer.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Adherents split between vegetarians like Reclus and others; no common position.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Berkman says the rich live on workers' labour; duty of charity does not fix this, and they demand expropriation instead.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: They are committed to revolutionary activity and building organisation, though not through parliaments.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Malatesta says teachers and priests are used to teach obedience, but there is no statement on mass media.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nationality as a qualification for office contradicts their opposition to nation-states and borders.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Territorial claims by states are nationalism, which they oppose.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: They oppose rule of any group over another, so mandated leadership is not their model.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: They oppose fascism but also constitutions and states, so adherents would not endorse this framing.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its negative rests on rejecting the idea that other civilizations should develop their own forms of government, and the statement now asks only whether Western institutions are unsuitable for some civilizations.

reviewHistory.rationale: They reject Western states as much as others; the claim of civilisational fit is not theirs.

reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

military-guardian-role.rationale: Malatesta says government rests on force, and a political role for armed forces would extend it.

office-by-exam.rationale: Offices of rule are abolished; administration is delegated work.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategic industries should be commonly owned by workers and communes, so state blocking of foreign buyers defends national capital and borders, which they reject.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Delegates bound by those who chose them and removable at any time are the anarchist alternative to representatives.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Kropotkin's principle of need means support for the old is a common provision, not private savings.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land is common property held by use, in Kropotkin's words close to this principle.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: They reject both the state and parliaments, so a parliamentary budget check is only a lesser evil.

single-official-language.rationale: Federalism and cultural freedom oppose enforced uniformity.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: They reject private land ownership for anyone, native or foreign.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Kropotkin criticises production of absolutely injurious goods and rich men's luxuries, though he also wanted everyone to enjoy comforts.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: States arming proxies is militarism; some anarchists support insurgents but not through governments.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Imperial control by force over another state is the domination they oppose; this follows from their opposition to militarism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: They oppose extending state power to control media and civil society.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: State incentives for births are a government tool; no stated view.

job-guarantee.rationale: Wage labour is to be abolished; a state job guarantee preserves wages and the state, though it would satisfy some demands.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Malatesta's rejection of government and law means no general duty to obey.

non-intervention.rationale: They oppose state interventions but support solidarity with insurgents elsewhere, so not absolute.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Déjacque opposed the nuclear family, and the ideology rejects state-conferred rights, so legal marriage is rejected.

public-access-to-information.rationale: They oppose secrecy of power, but the demand is for abolition of government not a right to its files.

local-production.rationale: Kropotkin's free agro-industrial communes aim at decentralised production close to need.

informal-organisation.rationale: Insurrectionary anarcho-communists favour affinity groups against organisations, while platformists favour a unified federation, so adherents are split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: They reject the nation-state's claim to supremacy and favour federation across frontiers.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The overview, citing Berkman, keeps personal possession (your watch) while the factory belongs to the people, separating this from a total abolition of ownership.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Anarchists reject hierarchy and patriotism between states, and Berkman condemns war and national rivalries; ritual tribute to a leading power is contrary to free, equal federation.

defeat-communism.rationale: Adherents are themselves communists who want communism without a state; they oppose attacking it, though they also oppose Leninist state communism.

religion-illusion.rationale: Malatesta and the anarchist tradition treat religion as a prop of authority and a product of ignorance and misery that will fade with liberty and education, though not purely as consolation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Kropotkin credits capitalism's machinery and productive power as the basis for abundance, but anarchists mostly stress exploitation; adherents are split.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anarcho-communists tie women's subordination to property, the state and wage dependence, and see equality as part of social revolution.

socialized-care.rationale: Communal kitchens, nurseries and shared domestic work follow from communal provision, but the sources read do not stress it and adherents favour voluntary rather than public provision.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Anarcho-communists are internationalists who reject nationalism and state language policy; purging words by policy is contrary to free agreement.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Kropotkin's programme is decentralised, self-governing communes that hold land and production in common, combining agriculture and industry.

majority-settlement.rationale: Anarcho-communists oppose nationalism and state-led assimilation or colonisation, and see patriotism as a tool of rulers.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Anarchists are internationalist and reject nations and states as the bearers of rights, so a people's tie to land does not outrank the claims of those living there now.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Rejecting state coercion over personal life and the criminal law as an instrument of authority, adherents oppose criminalising consensual relations.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Suppressing opposition is the practice of the state and dictatorship that the ideology rejects, and it criticised the Bolsheviks for exactly this.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Adherents are anti-clerical and oppose any state enforcing religion; punishing blasphemy would be authority at its worst.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Anti-imperialism and internationalism follow from rejecting exploitation and the state; colonial rule for the ruler's benefit is exploitation.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Direct self-management by those affected, in workplaces and communities through federated assemblies, is the core of the ideology's alternative to the state.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The ideology sits firmly on the revolutionary left and sees capitalists and workers as opposed classes whose best ideas cannot be merged.

alienated-labor.rationale: Wage labour is condemned as wage slavery that cuts workers off from the product and control of their work, and free creative work is the aim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Atheism and the rejection of all authority are central, as in Bakunin's anarchist critique of God and the state.

social-market-economy.rationale: Both markets and wage relations are rejected, and the state-regulated compromise is rejected as well; production and distribution are to be organised in common.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Anti-militarism and abolishing the state's standing army are central, though adherents accept voluntary revolutionary militias in a revolution.

rich-first.rationale: Equality and abolition of class privilege are central; letting some get rich first contradicts them.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-militarism and rejection of rival states point to refusing alignment with great-power blocs, though adherents would prefer no state armies at all.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anarchist writers such as Berkman argue that formal liberties are hollow under capitalism because the wealthy control the means of expression.

racial-franchise.rationale: Anarcho-communism is internationalist and rejects rule by any group over another, so it opposes racial limits on political rights.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Kropotkin's case for common ownership rests on the view that private accumulation of wealth gives some people power over the rest, so anarcho-communists treat it as a threat to freedom.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Anarcho-communists want the state abolished and favour free, voluntary association, so a state programme of promoting atheism, though many adherents are atheists, runs against their principles.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Malatesta's Anarchy argues that government, police and prisons exist to protect privilege and that order should come from free agreement and voluntary cooperation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The classical sources predate the idea; adherents would care about extinction but no stated position makes it a top policy priority and they disagree with state-led priorities.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Anarcho-communists reject authority in all relations, including marriage, and favour free union between equals; the overview covers their view of the family.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Anarcho-communism opposes the state, army and hierarchical discipline, so state-organised drilled youth contradicts it.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The movement is anti-militarist and opposes state armies, though it does not use the sovereignty argument.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Kropotkin attacks rent, interest and profit as unearned and wants common ownership, though anarcho-communists go further and reject wages for distribution by need.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Malatesta accepted revolutionary and defensive violence as necessary against oppression, and the movement is not pacifist.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The movement is internationalist and rejects nationalism and the state, so it does not view nations as continuous from antiquity.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The movement is internationalist and rejects the sacralised nation and state, though it honours its own movement's dead.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Anarcho-communism is secular and materialist, treating politics as class and social struggle against domination.

culture-before-state.rationale: The movement seeks to abolish the state rather than build one, so the question of sequencing does not arise.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The movement is secular and has no test for religious texts.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The movement is internationalist and rejects national divisions, favouring common ownership by all communities rather than by a national majority.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Berkman criticises the Leninist state for ruling over workers, and holds that workers' own free organisations must run society.

second-chamber.rationale: Malatesta rejects parliaments and legislatures, and a federation of communes has no second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: Means of production are held in common by free communes and associations, though they stress federations as well as localities.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement envisages free federations of communes whose delegates coordinate while the decisions stay with the commune.

person-over-state.rationale: Malatesta and Berkman oppose the state as an instrument of oppression and defend individual freedom within voluntary association.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Malatesta and Berkman criticise religion as a prop of authority, and the movement is secular.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Communes federate freely, and Malatesta rejects government, so a national legislature holding revocable powers over regions has no place.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Malatesta and Berkman oppose armies, war and patriotism, so they would not endorse state armed forces even for defence.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Anarcho-communists treat nations as products of states and reject nationalism and patriotism, so a nation defined by shared language and history is not a political unit they endorse.

communal-electorates.rationale: They reject voting and representative government altogether, and see religion as a private matter, so separate religious electorates are doubly opposed.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Berkman and the movement treat patriotism as a trick of the ruling class, so fears of foreign plots against "my country" are rejected as nationalist propaganda.

arms-reduction.rationale: They want standing armies and war abolished, so reducing arms agrees in direction, though they reject the frame of "national safety".

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Anarchist communists reject the state and want the people armed, as in Makhno's and Spain's militias; follows from abolishing the state.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Anti-militarism is central: wars between states are fought for rulers, and soldiers should refuse.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Anarchist communists value collective struggle but doubt that bargaining with employers can do more than patch the wage system they want to abolish; adherents differ.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Anarchist communists hold that revolution must destroy the state, not use it, which is their break with Marxism.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Malatesta urged free experiment without a fixed plan, though Kropotkin and Berkman advocated communism as the goal; adherents lean to freedom of choice.

sacred-nation.rationale: Anarchist communists reject nationalism and the state and are internationalist and mostly atheist.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Kropotkin roots mutual aid in human nature, but anarchists generally deny a fixed nature and reject sacred limits; adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Malatesta and the tradition reject government and parliamentary politics, so a workers' party aiming at office is refused.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Anarcho-communists abolish the state and its laws, so no religious interpretation would hold legal precedence.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Malatesta argues that voting and majority rule leave government and property in place, so elections cannot alone make society free.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Kropotkin wants wages and money abolished and goods by need, not a state-managed income top-up.

women-suffrage.rationale: Anarcho-communists support equality of women and men, though they reject voting and office as means of change.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Anarchists oppose religion alongside the state, and Malatesta and Berkman treat it as an instrument of authority.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Kropotkin wants land and resources held in common and distributed by need, so a right to private ownership by first claim is rejected.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anarcho-communists reject the state and its bureaucracy whoever owns the property, and opposed the Bolshevik state.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Berkman condemns patriotism as a tool of rulers and the movement is internationalist, so a sacred duty to ancestral land is rejected.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Malatesta treats police and government as the gendarme of property and Berkman traces crime to social conditions, so state killing without trial is rejected.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Kropotkin holds all wealth, land included, belongs to everyone and calls for expropriation, though under communism no one owes compensation, since nothing is privately owned.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Anarcho-communists reject rulers and organise through free federations of communes and associations, not a leader dealing with the masses.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Malatesta calls government the gendarme of property, and anarcho-communists want no state favours to the propertied.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Anarcho-communists are secular and Malatesta attacks religion's role in domination, though they reject offices and parties altogether.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Kropotkin and Berkman treat private fortunes as the product of exploiting collective labour, so a distribution is judged by need and exploitation rather than by whether each exchange was voluntary.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Kropotkin argues that machinery and shared work can give everyone ample leisure, with the gains shared by all rather than by owners.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Berkman treats patriotism as a tool of rulers that sets workers against each other in war, so anarchist communists reject it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Berkman's critique of the Bolshevik state and the movement's rejection of wages and markets make party-led market socialism contrary to anarchist communism.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Distribution by need is central; cutting support for the poor contradicts mutual aid, even though they distrust welfare delivered by the state. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

former-empire-equal-treatment.rationale: Imperial influence is opposed as a state project. (Carried over from former-empire-influence, "A country should cultivate political and cultural influence in regions once ruled by its predecessor empire.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: Agriculture and industry should be combined in the same communities rather than split between countryside and town.
missingStatements.rationale: Kropotkin's preface states the problem as combining agriculture with industry on communistic principles in free agro-industrial communes.

missingStatements.text: Personal belongings should remain private while the means of production are held in common.
missingStatements.rationale: The overview, citing Berkman, keeps personal possession (your watch) while the factory belongs to the people, a defining line between this and a total abolition of ownership.

notes: Adherents split on whether work should be purely voluntary (Kropotkin, Bookchin) or an obligation for able adults (Makhno, Magon), and on organisation: platformists want a unified federation, insurrectionists prefer affinity groups. Many answers on topics the classical texts never addressed are low-confidence inferences from anti-statism, internationalism and distribution by need. Fetched pages were read only in part, as noted in each source.
